name: Cei
text: Cei is a figure in Welsh Arthurian stories and a comrade of Arthur and Bedwyr. Writers give him the patronymic ap Cynyr. Some render that name as vab Cynyr. Both forms mean son of Cynyr. He holds the post of seneschal in the household of Arthur. His character mixes courage with buffoonery. Early poetry such as the twelfth-century Black Book of Carmarthen portrays him as a grand and admirable hero. Later romances demote him to a surly steward whose conduct turns cruel and sometimes ridiculous. Even there he manages to set events in motion. English Arthurian narratives clearly draw on him for the knight Sir Kay.

okr.objective: Portray Cei as seneschal of Arthur, an early admired hero who later becomes surly, and the model for Sir Kay.
key_results: Names Cei a Welsh Arthurian figure and comrade of Arthur and Bedwyr
Gives the patronymic ap Cynyr or vab Cynyr, son of Cynyr
States Cei serves as seneschal of the household of Arthur
Contrasts the admired hero of early poetry with the surly steward of later romances
Identifies Cei as the model for Sir Kay in English narratives
